limits: The two Ghent test sessions were already viewed in the BOLA diagnostic; this is a diagnostic comparison, not a blind confirmatory test.
Only two test sessions are available; report per trace and do not infer statistical significance.
The Ghent collection is historical observed HTTP goodput, not controlled link capacity or a modern cellular sample.
The DQN was trained with seven candidates including an 8 kbps startup rung; this transfer ladder contains six candidates.
RobustMPC uses nominal bitrate-duration sizes for future chunks and constant predicted goodput over its five-chunk horizon.
The RobustMPC rollout approximates the environment's buffer cap and fixed RTT; it does not model transport protocol dynamics or request abandonment.
The objective is the project's log-bitrate QoE proxy, not VMAF, MOS, or human acceptance.
The first RobustMPC action is constrained by the same safety mask as the frozen DQN and highest-allowed rule.
